SUMMARY OF ESSENTIAL ELEMENTS OF CITING/REFEREE’S REPORT/INCIDENT FOOTAGE
Lifted the player, through the horizontal and dropped him on his head.
ESSENTIAL ELEMENTS OF OTHER EVIDENCE (e.g. medical reports)
FR8 was uninjured and able to play on.
SUMMARY OF PLAYER’S EVIDENCE
Player (“Fiji 92”) reviewed the video footage and accepted the RC and acknowledged the offence. Fiji
92 also noted that he was attempting to catch the player and not drop him, but was unable to hold
him. Before leaving the field of play, he apologised to FR8 and shook hands.
FINDINGS OF FACT
Fiji 92 accepted the RC and therefore we move to sanction.
Reg. 17.18 - Seriousness of the Incident
The first stage is to consider the seriousness of the incident to determine the entry point for the sanction. The
factors I have considered from Reg.17.18 include:
(a) The tackle was reckless.
(b) The ball carrier was lifted above the horizontal plane and landed on his head.
(c) The incident was avoidable but Fiji 92 does attempt to pull out of the tackle and catch the player as he
falls. He tries to lower the player safely but was unable to do so.
(d) FR8 was not ‘driven’ into the ground but rather was dropped.
(e) FR8 was uninjured.
In all the circumstances noted above, I believe that a low-end entry point of 6 weeks is appropriate.
17.19 Mitigating Factors
The second stage is to consider mitigating factors under Reg. 17.19. Factors I have considered are:
(a) Fiji 92 acknowledged the offence and accepted the RC.
(b) Fiji 92 has never received an RC in his rugby career.
(c) Fiji 92’s conduct at the hearing was very polite and respectful.
(d) Fiji 92 approached FR8 immediately after the incident and apologised.
(e) FR8 was uninjured.
For these reasons, I award full mitigation to Fiji 92 of 50% and, therefore, the sanction will be reduced to 3
matches.
In making this decision, I have considered the terms of Reg.17.19.3 which allows the JO to apply sanctions lower
than 50% of the lower end entry sanction where:
251130 Disciplinary Decision Siqila (Fiji) DXB 7s Page 2 of 6

(a) There are off-field mitigating factors; and
(b) The sanction would be wholly disproportionate to the level and type of offending.
In this case, I believe that Fiji 92’s acknowledgment and apology satisfy the first leg; however, I do not consider
the sanction to be wholly disproportionate. I believe that Fiji 92 did attempt to prevent FR8 from landing on his
head but the fact remains that Fiji 92 has a responsibility to ensure that FR8 landed safely, which he was not
able to do. Therefore, I do not consider that I am able to lower this sanction below 50% as I do not consider the
sanction to be wholly disproportionate and the sanction remains at 3 matches.
17.20 Aggravating Factors
I am not aware of any aggravating factors in this situation.
Matches / tournaments included in the sanction
Total sanction is 3 matches. Matches included in this sanction are:
1. HSBC SVNS Cape Town – 06.12.25; Fiji’s first pool match.
2. HSBC SVNS Cape Town – 06.12.25; Fiji’s second pool match.
3. HSBC SVNS Cape Town – 06.12.25; Fiji’s third pool match.
